submissionAttempts.body:
Host-contract version that applies to this workspace's integration: **1** (the exact-match host contract generation, not the package version).

Evidence (all local, mutually consistent):
1. Assembly handshake: `src/effects/runtime.ts:128` calls `assertHostContract(1)` inside `createPalimpsestEffects` (imported from `@ordarium/host-kit`), pinned as a literal and described as fail-closed with no tolerance layer.
2. Conformance test: `test/host_conformance.test.ts` CONF-A01 asserts `assertHostContract(1)` passes and `assertHostContract(2)` throws `HostContractMismatchError`; CONF-A02–A04 exercise the `hostPort` pass-through and runner against the pinned engine.
3. Shipped contract of the exact pinned version: `package.json` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` overrides pin all four `@ordarium/*` lines to release `ordarium-v1.3.1`; the installed `node_modules/@ordarium/core/package.json` is 1.3.1 and its shipped declaration `dist/src/host.d.ts` / `dist/src/host.js` export `HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1`; `assertHostContract` uses strict `!==` against that constant. `@ordarium/host-kit` 1.3.1 re-exports the same constant from core. So the pinned engine provides generation 1 and would reject a literal of 2.
4. Specifications: `docs/engineering/13-host-adapter-conformance-spec.md` states G18 was delivered as "contract generation 1" and that the literal `1` pins the contract generation palimpsest was built/tested against; `docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md` (r10, r19) records that there is no plan to move `HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION` to 2.

Why the competing "1.2.0" references do not change this: the 1.2.0 mentions in `07-ordarium-alignment.md` (r8) and `13-host-adapter-conformance-spec.md` §0 are the previous consumer pin on the **package-version axis** (the Ordarium release tarball palimpsest depended on at PLMP-CONF-1 delivery), not a host-contract generation. Package version and contract generation are different axes: the pin moved 1.2.0 → 1.3.1, but the generation stayed 1. Under this repo's own precedence rule (`docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md`), the published contract of the exact pinned version (rule 1) governs, and informational/historical alignment records are explanatory only and never override it (rule 3). A tolerated mismatch is explicitly disallowed as a compatibility layer.

No collaboration boundary contract overrides this: `collab_inbox` shows no contracts, and `contract_get` for the referenced `COMPAT-PAL-001` returns "no such contract".

Conclusion: the workspace integration targets host-contract generation **1** (via `@ordarium/*` 1.3.1). Changing the literal to 2 without a corresponding engine bump would fail closed at assembly with `HOST_CONTRACT_MISMATCH`.

finalAnswerPreview: I have enough local evidence to settle this without contacting the peer: the apparent disagreement is between two different version axes, not two candidate host-contract generations.
